last_transition_reason: The proof is complete and correct. It fixes an arbitrary index j in [0,D], handles the first-half case directly from the hypothesis, and in the second-half case shows D-j lies in [0, floor(D/2)] so that c_{D-j} is nonnegative; symmetry then gives c_j = c_{D-j} >= 0. This matches the lemma sketch exactly and uses no undeclared or forbidden dependencies.
latest_nl_proof:
Let j be any integer with 0 <= j <= D. We will prove that c_j >= 0.

If j <= floor(D/2), then c_j >= 0 by the given hypothesis on the first half of the coefficients.

Now suppose j > floor(D/2). We claim that D - j <= floor(D/2). Indeed, if D - j were also > floor(D/2), then, since j and D-j are integers, we would have j >= floor(D/2) + 1 and D - j >= floor(D/2) + 1. Adding these inequalities gives
D = j + (D-j) >= 2 floor(D/2) + 2.
But 2 floor(D/2) is either D or D-1, so 2 floor(D/2) + 2 > D, a contradiction. Therefore D-j <= floor(D/2). Also D-j >= 0 because j <= D.

Hence 0 <= D-j <= floor(D/2), so by the hypothesis on the first half of the coefficients we get c_{D-j} >= 0. Using the symmetry hypothesis, c_j = c_{D-j}, and therefore c_j >= 0.

Since j was arbitrary, we have proved that c_j >= 0 for every integer j with 0 <= j <= D. Equivalently, every coefficient of F(q) is nonnegative.
role_in_parent: Converts the half-range coefficient positivity from the bottleneck lemma into full coefficientwise nonnegativity using symmetry.
statement_nl: Let D be a nonnegative integer, and let F(q) = sum_{j=0}^D c_j q^j be a polynomial in Z[q]. Assume that c_j = c_{D-j} for every integer j with 0 <= j <= D, and assume also that c_j >= 0 for every integer j with 0 <= j <= floor(D/2). Then c_j >= 0 for every integer j with 0 <= j <= D. Equivalently, every coefficient of F(q) is nonnegative.

domain_restrictions: F belongs to the polynomial ring over the integers.
The coefficients c_j are integers because F has integer coefficients.
The index j is always an integer.
In the symmetry assumption, j ranges from 0 to D inclusive.
In the first nonnegativity assumption, j ranges from 0 to floor of D divided by 2 inclusive.
The displayed expansion of F uses only coefficients c_0 through c_D.
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: If the coefficients of a polynomial over the integers are symmetric around degree D and the coefficients in the first half are nonnegative, then every coefficient is nonnegative.
quantifier_order: Fix a polynomial F in the polynomial ring over the integers, with coefficients c_0 through c_D.
For every integer j between 0 and D inclusive, c_j equals c_{D minus j}.
For every integer j between 0 and floor of D divided by 2 inclusive, c_j is nonnegative.
Therefore, for every integer j between 0 and D inclusive, c_j is nonnegative.
